title: David Becomes King
summary: Told of Saul's death, David tears his clothes and has the Amalekite who claims to have killed Saul put to death. He sings a lament, 'How are the mighty fallen,' for Saul and Jonathan. David is anointed king of Judah at Hebron, while Abner makes Saul's son Ish-bosheth king of Israel. Years of war follow; Joab kills Abner, two captains murder Ish-bosheth, and David has them executed. All the tribes then come to Hebron, and David is anointed king of Israel at thirty.

title: Jerusalem and the Ark
summary: David takes the stronghold of Zion from the Jebusites and makes Jerusalem his capital, with help from Hiram of Tyre, and twice defeats the Philistines in the valley of Rephaim. He sets the ark on a new cart, and when Uzzah steadies it he is struck dead, so David leaves it at Obed-edom's house. Three months later David dances before the LORD in a linen ephod as the ark enters Jerusalem, and Michal despises him; he answers that he will humble himself more.

title: The Davidic Covenant
summary: David, settled in his house, tells Nathan he wants to build a house for the ark, and Nathan first says to go ahead. That night the LORD tells Nathan that he has never asked for a house of cedar, but that he will make David a house: David's offspring will build a house for his name, and his throne will be established forever, with discipline for wrongdoing. David sits before the LORD, praises him, and prays that his word be established.

title: David's Wars and Kindness to Mephibosheth
summary: David defeats the Philistines, Moab, Zobah, Syria, Edom and Amalek, takes tribute, dedicates silver and gold to the LORD, and sets up officials. He asks if any of Saul's house remains to be shown kindness for Jonathan's sake, and Ziba brings Mephibosheth, lame in both feet, whom David restores to Saul's land and seats at his table. When Hanun of Ammon humiliates David's envoys, Joab and Abishai defeat the Ammonites and their Syrian allies.

title: David, Bathsheba and Uriah
summary: While Joab's army besieges Rabbah, David stays in Jerusalem, sees Bathsheba bathing, and sleeps with her. When she is pregnant, he calls her husband Uriah home from the war; Uriah refuses to go to his house while the ark and the army are in tents. David sends Uriah back with a letter telling Joab to place him where the fighting is fiercest, and he dies. David marries Bathsheba. Nathan's parable leads David to say 'I have sinned'; their child dies, and Solomon is born.

title: Amnon, Tamar and Absalom
summary: Amnon, David's son, pretends to be ill, has his half-sister Tamar bring him food, and rapes her, then hates her and sends her away. Tamar's brother Absalom takes her in and says nothing for two years, until he has Amnon killed at a sheepshearing feast and flees to Geshur. Joab sends a wise woman of Tekoah with a story that leads David to bring Absalom home, but David refuses to see him for two years, until Absalom has Joab's field burned and David finally kisses him.

title: Absalom's Rebellion
summary: Absalom wins the people's loyalty at the city gate and has himself proclaimed king at Hebron. David flees Jerusalem with his servants and Ittai the Gittite, and Hushai pretends to join Absalom to undermine Ahithophel's advice. In the forest of Ephraim David's men defeat Absalom's, Absalom's head catches in an oak, and Joab kills him despite David's order. David mourns, 'O my son Absalom,' until Joab rebukes him, and then returns across the Jordan.

title: Sheba's Revolt and the Gibeonites
summary: Sheba, a Benjamite, calls Israel to leave David, and Joab, after killing Amasa, besieges Sheba in Abel until a wise woman has Sheba's head thrown over the wall. A three-year famine is then traced to Saul's killing of the Gibeonites; David gives seven of Saul's descendants to them, and Rizpah guards the bodies. David has the bones of Saul and Jonathan reburied, and the chapter closes with battles against Philistine giants.

title: David's Song and Last Words
summary: After the LORD delivers David from his enemies, David sings a long song calling the LORD his rock, fortress and deliverer and praising God's help in battle; it closely parallels Psalm 18. His last words speak of a righteous ruler and an everlasting covenant. The chapter then lists David's mighty men and tells how three broke through the Philistine lines to bring David water from the well at Bethlehem, which he pours out to the LORD.

title: The Census and the Plague
summary: The LORD, angry with Israel, moves David to count the people, and Joab protests but carries it out, reporting 800,000 in Israel and 500,000 in Judah. David regrets it and is offered three punishments by the prophet Gad; he chooses three days of plague over famine or flight, and 70,000 die. When the angel stands at the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite, David asks that the punishment fall on him instead, buys the floor and oxen, builds an altar, and the plague stops.
